title: Open with contents, not with eyebrows
intent: Let the reader choose a section instead of walking a fixed sequence of labels.
when_to_use: the document has six or more sections and a reader who will not read all of them
sections can be entered in any order
when_not_to_use: the sequence is the argument and skipping breaks comprehension
the document is under three sections, where a contents block costs more than it saves
rules: the page opens with a contents list using the section titles as written, not paraphrases
the eyebrow count stays at or below one for every three sections, counting the hero as a section
no eyebrow is numbered, and no section carries a coded two part label
every contents entry links to an anchor that exists in the document
trade_off: A contents block spends the strongest screen on navigation instead of the first idea, and it commits the document to titled sections that survive editing.
failure_mode: The contents list drifts from the document: renamed sections, anchors that no longer resolve, and a list longer than the page it describes.

example.brief: Policy page with nine sections read selectively by different roles.
example.ruling: A contents block lists the nine titles as written with anchors, no eyebrows or numbered labels are used anywhere, and each section title is unique so the anchor set stays stable.
